Operating Characteristics for Quantitative Decisions Comparing Means

Source: R/f_design_plan_qtd_means.R
getOperatingCharacteristicsMeans.Rd

Computes frequentist or Bayesian decision probabilities, selected by the class of the quantitative design rule.

Usage

getOperatingCharacteristicsMeans(
  design,
  ...,
  numberOfSubjects,
  normalApproximation = TRUE,
  groups = 2,
  alternative = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
  stDev = 1,
  priorDist = NULL,
  controlMean = NULL
)

Arguments

design

A rule from getDesignQuantitative().

...

Additional arguments are checked for unknown names.

numberOfSubjects

Positive integer matrix with columns control, treatment; each row is a sample-size scenario.

normalApproximation

Frequentist option, currently TRUE. Omit for Bayes.

groups

Number of groups; currently two.

alternative

Finite vector of true treatment-minus-control effects.

stDev

Positive common SD or, for Bayes, two known SDs ordered control, treatment. Defaults to one. Sampling uncertainty of SDs is not modeled.

priorDist

Bayesian RBesT normMix prior on the effect or a list of two normMix priors ordered control, treatment. NULL selects mixnorm(c(1, 0, 100)). Only identity-link normal mixtures are supported.

controlMean

True control mean, required only with separate group priors.

Value

An OperatingCharcteristicsMeans object with the rule, assumptions and category-block probability data frame. Bayesian data additionally retain stDevControl and stDevTreatment; the scalar stDev facet is their root mean square.

Details

Bayesian calculations require RBesT. Single-component normal priors use the analytic conjugate normal calculation; normal mixtures use RBesT oc1S (effect prior) or oc2S (group priors). The effect-prior sampling variance is stDevControl^2/nControl + stDevTreatment^2/nTreatment. For group priors, the true treatment mean is controlMean + alternative.

RBesT mixture OCs use numerical decision-boundary searches and integration. Agreement with independent references is therefore approximate, typically around 1e-4 with the package defaults; exact threshold ties and near-boundary values require care. No t-based or unknown-variance Bayesian model is implied. Bayesian probabilities are conditional sampling OCs at fixed true effects, not prior-predictive probabilities. All explicit categories are validated for exclusion before the residual category is calculated.

There are six frequentist categories, or four Bayesian categories: Go, Indeterminate 1, Indeterminate 2 and Stop. Three-category plots merge the two intermediate categories. Sample-size scenarios, effect order and repeats are retained. Bayesian priors and controlMean are stored for summaries, sensitivity recalculation and getObjectRCode().

See also

getDesignQuantitative(), getOperatingCharacteristicsRates()

Examples

rule <- getDesignQuantitative(1)
getOperatingCharacteristicsMeans(rule, numberOfSubjects = matrix(c(20, 30), ncol = 2))

if (requireNamespace("RBesT", quietly = TRUE)) {
    bayes <- getDesignQuantitative(1, bayesian = TRUE)
    getOperatingCharacteristicsMeans(bayes,
        numberOfSubjects = matrix(c(20, 30), ncol = 2), alternative = c(0, 1, 2))
}
